catalysts.headline: Q3 2026 results: core EPS $1.92 (down from $2.34 a year earlier, which included a one-time rate-case true-up), GAAP EPS $1.88; revenue ~$4.89B, down from ~$5.75B; core EPS beat consensus (Zacks: $1.83 consensus, 4.9% beat; 24/7 Wall St cites $1.81 consensus); revenue missed consensus (Zacks $5.53B vs. 24/7 Wall St $5.34B); 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20 and 5-7% annual core EPS growth target through 2030 reaffirmed; YTD core EPS through Q3 is $4.89

catalysts.headline: Bloomberg reported Edison International/Southern California Edison is considering shutting off power for up to roughly 246,000 customers amid wildfire-risk conditions
catalysts.impact: Operational/PSPS-related disclosure amid ongoing Eaton Fire liability scrutiny

catalysts.headline: Muddy Waters alleged Southern California Edison showed reckless/willful disregard in the Eaton Fire, citing potential liability of at least $4B in fire-related damages and up to roughly $20B if a court found willful misconduct; alleges SCE knew for ~5 years its wildfire risk model could not adequately handle high-wind conditions. Edison said it is cooperating with investigations and denies negligence or wrongdoing.
catalysts.impact: Shares fell more than 3% that session

catalysts.headline: Muddy Waters short report alleging willful disregard in the Eaton Fire, with potential liability cited as high as ~$20B (as carried on file)
catalysts.impact: Not independently verified this session — could not locate a primary or news-wire confirmation before the search budget was exhausted

catalysts.headline: Muddy Waters alleges Edison/SCE acted with 'conscious' or 'willful' disregard in the Eaton Fire; says liability could reach ~$20B if willful misconduct is found (vs ~$4B base case)
Jefferies downgrade to Sell, price target cut to $42

Edison International's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q discloses that the county fire department and CAL FIRE issued reports in August 2026 pointing to an electrical arcing event on a de-energized, idle SCE transmission line as the Eaton Fire's probable ignition source; SCE states that, absent new evidence, its equipment was likely associated with the ignition. The filing also discloses that SCE exhausted its $1.0 billion of self-insurance recoveries for Eaton Fire losses as of 2026-02-11, that fines/penalties tied to the fire will not be recoverable from insurance, the Wildfire Fund, or electric rates, and that a state safety investigation and a Los Angeles County District Attorney investigation remain open (SCE says it sees no basis for a felony liability finding). Multiple individual, subrogation, and public-entity lawsuits remain pending against SCE and Edison International.
catalysts.impact: Clarifies the probable ignition cause and the exhaustion of self-insurance, while leaving total liability unquantified; keeps both SCE and the parent exposed to ongoing litigation and investigations
catalysts.note: Date reflects the 10-Q's reporting period (2026-09-30); the exact SEC filing date was not independently confirmed this session, but the content is new relative to the on-file record, which only captured the $9M after-tax settlement-charge figure from the same filing.

catalysts.headline: Eaton Fire settlement charge of $9M (after-tax) recorded cumulatively through Q3 2026; company states it still cannot estimate total Eaton Fire losses but says SCE has identified funding sources to resolve claims. Bellwether jury trials are set for January, May, and September 2027; SCE has filed a motion to continue the January 2027 trial to June 2027.
SCE announces additional community engagement opportunities ahead of Nov. 30 Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program deadline
UBS maintains Hold, price target $57

LA County Superior Court Judge Laura Seigle denied Edison International's motion for summary judgment seeking to be dropped from Eaton Fire litigation; the parent company had argued it had no ownership or control over the equipment at issue, but the judge found it had not met its burden of showing it bore no responsibility. The ruling is a denial of summary judgment, not a finding of liability.
catalysts.impact: Keeps Edison International (the parent, not just SCE) as a defendant exposed in Eaton Fire litigation

catalysts.headline: Morgan Stanley reiterates Sell, price target $60
Community meeting highlights continued participation and interest in SCE's Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program
Jefferies cuts price target $68 -> $53, keeps Hold
Truist Securities cuts price target $77 -> $63, keeps Hold
California Assembly declines to vote on SB 492 compromise; bill dies for the session without passing -- the version that stripped liability protections never became law

California Legislature's regular session ended without advancing Gov. Newsom's proposal to amend wildfire-liability reform (SB 492 amendment); SCE says the amended bill falls short and is pushing for a special legislative session before a Nov. 15 constitutional deadline for the Governor to act; CEO called the lack of action 'disappointing' and said a fallback to 2027 would be 'significant and costly'

catalysts.headline: California State Assembly revised SB 492, stripping out utility wildfire-liability shields and omitting Gov. Newsom's provision barring insurer subrogation suits against utilities; Mizuho cut EIX to Neutral from Outperform, Argus cut to Hold from Buy
SCE calls for comprehensive wildfire reform to protect communities and keep bills affordable

Edison International reported Q2 2026 results: core EPS $1.54 (core earnings $592M) vs. $0.97 YoY, beating a ~$1.18 consensus; GAAP EPS $1.39 (net income $534M vs. $343M YoY); reaffirmed FY2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90–$6.20; reported more than 2,200 Eaton Fire compensation offers totaling over $775M, with the company stating it still lacks enough claims/settlement data to set a GAAP low-end liability estimate
catalysts.impact: Core earnings beat; Eaton Fire liability remains unquantified under GAAP pending more claims data

catalysts.headline: Q2 2026: core EPS $1.54 (vs $0.97 Y/Y), GAAP EPS $1.39, revenue $4.357B (missed $4.72B estimate); reaffirmed FY2026 core EPS guidance $5.90-$6.20

conflicts: Q3 2026 consensus EPS: Zacks cites $1.83 consensus (4.9% beat); 24/7 Wall St cites $1.81 consensus. Both readings recorded verbatim; not averaged.
Q3 2026 consensus revenue: Zacks cites ~$5.53B consensus; 24/7 Wall St cites ~$5.34B consensus.
notes: Key open item as of 2026-11-11 (today): a Nov. 15, 2026 constitutional deadline for the Governor to call a special legislative session on wildfire liability reform was referenced in Oct/early-Nov coverage, but no source confirms the outcome yet (the date has not yet passed at time of this research). The Wildfire Recovery Compensation Program had scaled to >3,200 offers totaling ~$1.1B as of the Q3 call (up from ~$775M the prior quarter), ahead of a Nov. 30, 2026 program deadline. CPUC approved SCE's 2026-2028 Wildfire Mitigation Plan (OEIS approval referenced in search results, exact date not confirmed); ~90% of distribution lines in high-fire-risk areas reported hardened. Recommend a follow-up pass after Nov. 15-16 to capture the special-session outcome, and direct SEC EDGAR/Edison IR access (sec.gov and most financial-data sites were unreachable in this sandbox) for market cap/P/E and Eaton Fire litigation docket status.
